QF.id: Role of RTAs in Mutual Fund Transactions_30

question.text: Rajesh submits a mutual fund purchase application from a B-30 city. Which of the following statements about additional TER for B-30 inflows is correct?

answer.text: No additional TER is permitted for B-30 cities under current regulations
Additional TER applies only if the investor is a first-time mutual fund investor
Additional TER and incentive are permitted for B-30 inflows, and inflows are treated as retail only where the transaction is up to Rs.2,00,000 per transaction
Additional TER of 0.50% applies to all B-30 transactions regardless of amount

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports two points: (1) AMCs are allowed to charge an additional TER and pay an additional incentive for inflows from B-30 (Beyond top 30) cities, and (2) such inflows qualify as "retail" only where the per-transaction amount is up to Rs.2,00,000. This is what makes Option C the supported statement. The Trap: The exact numeric cap (such as 0.30%) on the additional B-30 TER is not supported by the workbook pages checked and must not be stated as a fact without a current SEBI circular citation. Treat retail B-30 inflows as those up to Rs.2,00,000 per transaction. Note: The B-30 incentive structure is meant to encourage geographical penetration of mutual funds beyond the top 30 cities. Any specific TER cap should be cross-checked against the latest SEBI circular before quoting it to clients.
